title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing benchmark results vs customer's baseline provider. Redwood showed lower tail latency and higher throughput in most configs; discussed tuning (batch size, KV cache, quantization) and next steps to run 99th percentile tests and share full dashboards. Agreed to run additional benchmark with caching and extend pilot window.
next_steps: Redwood to share full benchmark spreadsheet + perf dashboard link
SE to run focused 99th-percentile run with KV cache enabled and send results
Customer to provide production traffic trace and sample prompts
Discuss pilot extension and pricing after next benchmark
action_items: Jamie Park (Redwood) - Share full benchmark sheet and Grafana link - due 2025-03-21
Samir Patel (Redwood SE) - Run 99th percentile run with KV cache + int8 profile and report - due 2025-03-24
Leo Martins (AtlasAI) - Provide representative production traffic trace and sample prompts - due 2025-03-20
Ruth Chang (AtlasAI) - Confirm pilot extension decision and budget - due 2025-03-28
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: ok folks thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync, we have a packed agenda, mainly benchmark review vs the baseline you ran last week
[00:12] Ruth: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we got your slides, wanna focus on latency and throughput numbers, and then discuss any tuning we should try
[00:20] Samir: cool, i'll kick off with the headline numbers, quick note transcription might butcher some product names, so apologies in advance
[00:26] Samir: for the small-seq workload (avg seq len ~128 tokens) our P50 is ~45 ms vs BaselineCloud 72 ms, P95 is ~210 ms vs BaselineCloud 420 ms, throughput measured as tokens/sec was about 12,400 for Redwood vs ~7,200 for BaselineCloud under the same virtual users
[00:46] Ruth: wow that P95 gap is big, is that with caching on?
[00:50] Samir: good call, those numbers are with caching disabled to keep apples-to-apples; when we enable prefix/KV caching we see another ~20-30% tail improvement in practice, especially for repetitive prompts
[01:05] Leo: ok, curious about GPU utilization and cost tradeoffs, your slides showed lower util but higher efficiency?
[01:12] Samir: right, baseline was pegging GPU util at ~85% which looks efficient superficially but indicates they're saturating in a way that increases queuing and tail latency. Redwood runs at ~60-65% util on the same instance type because we do more efficient kernel selection and continuous batching/prefetching which gives better latency profile and costs are lower per-token - rough cost we calculated was $0.0008 per token for our config vs $0.0014 for BaselineCloud (estimations, we'll share the sheet)
[01:38] Priya: that cost delta is compelling but we need to validate on our long-tail prompts, not just the benchmark set
[01:44] Samir: agree, that's why next run will use your production trace - it captures tail behavior and weird sequences
[01:50] Jamie: quick clarification on configs: the benchmark used the same model family (open-llm-7b-int8 like config), int8 quantization was enabled for both vendors where available; batch size tuning on Redwood was 8 for latency-first, and we also tried a throughput-oriented profile with batch=32 where throughput rose to ~18k tokens/sec but P95 increased a bit
[02:13] Ruth: so with batch32 latency got worse, is there a recommended sweet spot?
[02:17] Samir: usually for interactive SLOs we recommend batch 8-12; depends on your QPS and SLOs. also persistent KV cache helps a ton for repeated prefixes - that one will keep P95 down without sacrificing throughput much
[02:30] Leo: any notes on cold start or warmup? we saw some spikes during the first minute in our tests
[02:35] Samir: yes cold-starts matter - we measure warmup windows and suggest a short steady-state run before measuring. also session pinning and a small reserved pool reduces cold spikes, that's part of Redwood Dedicated if you want reservation
[02:48] Ruth: we are evaluating hosted first, but dedicated is on the table if numbers hold up and security checks out
[02:54] Jamie: speaking of security, we've uploaded SOC2 summary and the audit logs doc, we'll share the link in the follow-up. any outstanding compliance blockers?
[03:03] Priya: SAML SSO and KMS integration are blockers for some of our stakeholders, and data residency for EU customers is a question
[03:11] Jamie: we have SAML, KMS integrations, and region controls - we'll include config notes and a short runbook for VPC/on-prem options
[03:20] Ruth: back to benchmarks, can you walk through the P95 distribution, looks like Baseline had pronounced spikes at certain percentiles
[03:27] Samir: yep, baseline's P95 and P99 are much higher; their P99 occasionally hits 1.2s on loads where ours is ~480-520 ms. those spikes line up with queuing events when the backend schedules big batches. we can reproduce with high concurrency synthetic tests, which we'll run next
[03:45] Leo: how about sequence length variability? our product has bursts of 1k token sessions sometimes
[03:50] Priya: (overlap) yeah we see both short chat messages and long doc summaries
[03:54] Samir: long sequences change the memory profile - for long documents we recommend a chunking strategy and using model variants optimized for long context. for the POC we tested up to 2k tokens and saw latency grow roughly linearly; we can produce a chart
[04:07] Jamie: are there any red flags from your side, Ruth?
[04:10] Ruth: not yet, just want to make sure the benchmark methodology is sound and reproducible
[04:15] Samir: methodology notes: identical hardware SKU, same model weights, same batch generators, seeded RNG where appropriate, we captured wall-clock and internal queueing times. caveats noted in the sheet - sampling variation is ~5-8% for p50, larger for tails
[04:30] Ruth: ok, next steps from me: we'll share a traffic trace and a list of heavy prompts by EOD Thursday
[04:36] Leo: and we'll request a run with KV cache enabled and compare
[04:40] Samir: yep Samir will run that; also i'll enable the int8 specialized kernels and produce a throughput vs latency curve, plus GPU metrics (SM util, memory allocation, stalls)
[04:51] Jamie: also discuss pilot extension - are you all aligned to extend the POC by two weeks if the next run looks good?
[04:58] Ruth: probably yes, need to loop in finance but leaning yes
[05:02] Jamie: ok last bit, questions?
[05:05] Priya: what's the risk of model accuracy regressions with int8?
[05:09] Samir: small, we ran eval sets and saw negligible deltas for many model families; we also keep float16 variants if you need stricter quality checks, and Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles per workload
[05:20] Ruth: please include eval metrics with the next deliverable
[05:23] Jamie: will do. i'll send the benchmark sheet, grafana link, and compliance attachments after the call. thanks everyone
[05:30] Ruth: thanks, bye
[05:32] [call ends]
